summary.text: CA9 has the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1: 7.787) and is carried by RCC cells in two single-cell datasets (tumour-cell share 0.976 and 0.981). Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. It stays in the convergence top 10 in 0.894 of random re-weightings. It is not prognostic in TCGA (Cox padj 0.933) and is not a DepMap dependency, so it is a targeting and imaging handle rather than a functional vulnerability.

NNMT is the strongest dual target-and-biomarker candidate. It is up in tumour (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709) and tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256). It is prognostic in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), and its protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort (log2FC 4.776). RCC cells dominate its expression in both single-cell datasets. Literature calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential target, but it has no clinical drug, so the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

CD70 is a surface antigen where omics, literature and clinical programmes agree: tumour-up RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), TCGA-KIRC replication (log2FC 7.09), a purity-1 log2FC of 4.278, and cusatuzumab at PHASE_2. Its ADC suitability (0.746) is the highest among the known targets. The caveat is that immune cells hold 0.654 of its tumour transcripts, so tumour-cell restriction is not established and the ADC and immune uses must be kept apart.

Much of the overall convergence top 25 consists of proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PIGR), and PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1 lead the biomarker profile. These are prognostic loss biomarkers, not targets. VHL is the driver (mutated in 247 of 511 tumours), and the actionable route downstream of it is HIF-2alpha (EPAS1, belzutifan at APPROVAL). EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal, and in single-cell data its transcripts sit mainly in endothelium. No omics-convergent target is a selective dependency, and no candidate separates the IMmotion150 treatment arms.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-vs-normal omics split the candidates into two groups. CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 are up at RNA and protein and replicate in TCGA-KIRC, which fits the hypoxia- and glycolysis-driven state that follows VHL loss. PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1 and PPP1R1A are down at RNA and protein, mark loss of normal tubule identity and are prognostic in TCGA. Higher expression is protective for PCK1 and ALDH6A1 but adverse for PSAT1 and PPP1R1A.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.399, protein log2FC -1.925), is lost in 0.355 of tumours and has a positive copy-number-to-expression correlation (cis rho 0.525). Higher expression is protective (Cox log HR -0.554). The copy-number link gives a plausible genomic cause for its loss.

FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 6.431) and is gained in 0.573 of tumours (cis rho 0.309), so copy gain is a likely contributor. It is a robust target-profile gene with no literature in the corpus.

literature.text: Literature and data converge most clearly for CA9 (tumour-enriched, PET imaging proof of concept), CD70 (overexpressed in RCC, minimal in normal tissue, radiotracers in development) and NNMT (prognostic, with selective chemical inhibitors). SLC16A3 has one mechanistic paper on lactate-driven immune evasion through GPR81. Most claims rest on single retrospective, bioinformatic or preclinical studies, and both translational papers call for prospective validation. SCARB1 and PIGR have no literature relations in the corpus, so their ranks are data-driven.

ALDOB literature agrees with the data on direction: an IHC cohort shows it diminished in tumour relative to adjacent tissue and proposes it as a prognostic biomarker. The same papers call it a potential immunotherapy target, but loss of expression is not directly druggable, so the target wording is speculative.

MT1G is the clearest literature contradiction. It is reported low in ccRCC tissue, yet functional work links high expression to advanced stage, poorer prognosis and growth and metastasis through lipid-droplet accumulation. Its role is unresolved.

external.text: EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target: belzutifan is at APPROVAL and its Open Targets association score is 0.4871. It is the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061, not significant at 0.05). Its low expression-driven convergence rank despite clinical validation is the main disagreement between the data-driven ranking and clinical reality.

Open Targets and UniProt split the tumour-up candidates by modality. CA9 and CD70 are membrane proteins with antibody programmes (girentuximab PHASE_3, cusatuzumab PHASE_2), and ENPP3 had the ADC AGS-16C3F at PHASE_2. SCARB1 is a membrane receptor with a genetic association (0.519) but no drug, and NNMT has no drug. VHL has the top Open Targets ccRCC association (0.6466) but is a tumour suppressor and not directly druggable.

MTOR is an established target with approved and late-stage inhibitors. All ccRCC lines depend on it (fraction 1.0, mean effect -1.52), but it is common essential, so the dependency signals toxicity risk rather than tumour selectivity. It is also recurrently mutated (37 of 511 patients).

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic at single-cell resolution: 54.7% of RCC cells express it and RCC cells carry 0.976 of tumour transcripts. Paired by donor, it is higher in tumour cells than in proximal tubule (log2FC 7.739, padj 0.0189). The attribution replicates in the second single-cell dataset (tumour-cell share 0.981, tumour vs tubule log2FC 8.522).

Cell attribution replicates for NNMT (tumour-cell shares 0.97 and 0.948) and for the loss marker PCK1 (0.964 and 0.969), but not for SCARB1 or SLC16A3. SCARB1 is dominated by myeloid cells in Li 2022 (tumour share 0.336) and by RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.582). SLC16A3 is dominated by T/NK cells in Li 2022 (0.327) and by RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.809). Their tumour increase is reproducible, but which cells carry it is unresolved. CD70 is not a bulk-only tumour gene either: immune cells hold 0.654 of its tumour transcripts.

Several familiar targets are not tumour-cell genes. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of tumour transcripts). EPAS1 transcripts sit mostly in endothelium (share 0.365), with only 0.051 in RCC cells, and its RNA purity-1 log2FC is 0.46. CXCR4 is held by CD8 T cells (0.563). MET is mainly in RCC cells (0.935), but its tumour-vs-tubule difference is not significant (padj 0.069).

spatial.text: In Visium sections RCC carries a composition-corrected share of 0.999 of CA9 transcripts. High-CA9 spots are surrounded by RCC (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017), with only slight macrophage enrichment (0.099). CA9 marks the tumour compartment in situ, consistent with its single-cell and purity profile.
KDR is explained in situ by endothelium (composition-corrected share 0.99), confirming it as a microenvironment (angiogenesis) target rather than a tumour-cell target.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) scores rank candidate sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine), its model mean pLDDT is 76.56, and recall in the top pockets is only 0.221, which makes it a weak, small site.

The highest-ranked sites belong to non-tumour genes. KDR's best site scores 0.841 (361.1 A3, 7 accessible lysines) and the macrophage gene GAL3ST4 scores 0.7874 (819.7 A3, no ligand-site validation). COL23A1's model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91) and its site scores 0.2342, so antibody tractability is more plausible for it. These rank sites only; no glue is implied.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the lead novel candidate (novelty 0.767). RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts, it has no clinical drug, and it replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives purity extrapolation (log2FC 4.88 at purity 1). RAB42 follows (novelty 0.705, RCC share 0.627, TCGA log2FC 4.371, 3.189 at purity 1). Neither shows a selective DepMap dependency.

In the stroma track, OLFML2A is carried by fibroblasts (0.647 of tumour transcripts) and replicates in TCGA (log2FC 2.372, 1.527 at purity 1), but colon expression (nTPM 27.9) is an off-tumour risk. JAG2 is endothelial (0.487 share), replicates (log2FC 1.549) and survives purity extrapolation (1.061).

The immune track is mostly immune genes, and purity extrapolation separates them. GAL3ST4 (macrophages 0.972) keeps a small positive change at purity 1 (log2FC 0.401) and is adverse in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.177). LILRB4 is up in TCGA (log2FC 3.7) but only 0.508 at purity 1, so its increase is infiltration-driven. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses without functional or dependency evidence.

validation.text: Protein calls replicate in the confirmatory DIA cohort for SCARB1 (log2FC 2.334), NNMT (4.776), SLC16A3 (3.551), PSAT1 (-3.946) and PCK1 (-4.819). That strengthens all five. CA9 was too sparse to test there, which is not a failure to replicate. TCGA-KIRC replicates every up-regulated target, but only the loss markers and NNMT carry prognosis.

The genetic and functional layers weaken the target case. VHL (247 of 511) and PBRM1 (185 of 511) are the recurrent drivers, but none of the convergent targets is mutated recurrently or is a selective DepMap dependency. Only EPAS1 shows a selective signal (selectivity 0.3), and MTOR's dependency is common essential. The purity check separates tumour-intrinsic genes (CA9 purity-1 log2FC 7.787, NNMT 5.256) from infiltration: FCGR3A is almost purely immune (immune-cell share 0.999).

robustness.text: In the target profile, SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1-8), CA9 (0.941, 1-13), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 (0.88) and NNMT (0.88) keep their places under random re-weighting. PNCK sits just below them but almost never enters the top 10 (p_top10 0.004), so its position depends on the chosen weights. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robust (p_top10 0.894, p_top25 0.983).

In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 is the most stable candidate (p_top10 0.986, interval 1-4), followed by PCK1 (0.889), SLC6A19 (0.881) and PPP1R1A (0.8). DUSP9 (p_top10 0.398, upper bound 117) and L1CAM (0.297, upper bound 88) are weight-dependent and should be read as secondary.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, no gene separates the two main arms. CD70 is the strongest lead: higher expression is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (log HR per SD -0.383, adjusted p 0.166), with an arm difference of -0.121 (adjusted p 0.927). CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib (-0.336, adjusted p 0.332). These are associations from arms of about 90 patients, not predictive markers.

For the loss biomarkers, PCK1 trends towards earlier progression on the combination (log HR per SD 0.22, adjusted p 0.572), and PSAT1 has only single-arm and small-trial estimates. NNMT has no IMmotion150 arm estimate, so its treatment relevance cannot be judged.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the only candidate checked that is flagged as a subgroup target: it is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours (TCGA RNA 1.148, adjusted p 7.18e-7) and lower in ccB than ccA (protein -0.52). SCARB1 is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours at RNA but not at protein (adjusted p 0.113), and PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours at RNA only. EPAS1 defines the ccA/ccB split (TCGA RNA -0.935). Subgroup differences in immune genes can reflect infiltration rather than tumour-cell change.

adc.text: CD70 (ADC suitability 0.746) and CA9 (0.647) are the known-target controls, and both score well. CA9 has no kidney staining but stains stomach, and CD70 lacks staining data, so its vital-organ safety cannot be judged. SLC16A3 scores high (0.725), but it has 12 transmembrane segments and only 66 extracellular residues, so an antibody epitope is doubtful. ENPP3 and SCARB1 stain normal kidney, and SCARB1 reaches only 7.1 percent of tumour cells in the weakest donors. NNMT is intracellular (suitability 0.25).

immune.text: FCGR3A is an immune-cell gene (immune-cell share 0.999, rho with the immune score 0.795), so it marks hot, infiltrated tumours rather than tumour cells. CD70 sits between the two: immune cells hold 0.654 of its transcripts and it correlates with CD8 T cells (rho 0.278). NNMT is the tumour-cell control (immune-cell share 0.015).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge on CA9, CD70 and NNMT, which are up in tumour, replicated, purity-robust and literature-supported. CA9 and CD70 also have clinical antibody programmes. SCARB1 and SLC16A3 are the most robust data-driven targets and replicate at protein, but they lack ccRCC literature and their cell attribution is inconsistent. The main disagreement is EPAS1, which is clinically validated and the only selective dependency but ranks low on expression.

targets.rationale: Strongest convergence: tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein, TCGA replication (log2FC 9.712), tumour-intrinsic in single cells (share 0.976) and in situ, girentuximab at PHASE_3, and the most robust candidate (convergence p_top10 0.894). It is a targeting and imaging handle, not a dependency or prognostic marker.

Tumour-intrinsic increase (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301), protein replication in the confirmatory cohort (log2FC 4.776) and literature support. It has no clinical drug and is intracellular, so the target call is for a small molecule.

Surface antigen with tumour-up RNA and protein, TCGA replication (log2FC 7.09), clinical antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2) and the highest ADC suitability among known targets (0.746). Placed below NNMT because immune cells hold 0.654 of its transcripts.

Top of the target profile and the most robust there (p_top10 0.968). It replicates in TCGA (log2FC 3.989) and at protein (confirmatory log2FC 2.334). Ranked below the first three because it has no literature or drug, normal kidney staining, and cell attribution that does not replicate.

MCT4 lactate transporter, up at RNA (log2FC 3.435) and protein (log2FC 2.279), replicated at protein (confirmatory log2FC 3.551), robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.881), with a mechanistic immune-evasion paper. A small-molecule rather than an antibody target, given its few extracellular residues.
Tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 3.895) and protein (log2FC 1.544), TCGA replication (log2FC 5.557) and a prior ADC (AGS-16C3F PHASE_2). Normal kidney staining is the main safety concern.

Included despite its low expression-driven rank because it is the validated ccRCC target (belzutifan at APPROVAL) and the only selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3). Its transcripts sit mainly in endothelium in single-cell data.
Most robust biomarker (p_top10 0.986). It is down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein, replicated in the confirmatory cohort (log2FC -3.946) and prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43).
Down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein, with protein loss replicated (confirmatory log2FC -4.819), protective prognosis (Cox log HR -0.415) and tumour-cell attribution in both single-cell datasets.
Down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein, with a copy-loss cause (loss frequency 0.355, cis rho 0.525) and the strongest protective prognosis among the loss markers (Cox log HR -0.554).
Robust in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.881), down in TCGA (log2FC -3.221) and protective (Cox log HR -0.456), with one supporting tumour-suppressive literature report.
Second in the overall convergence ranking, down in TCGA (log2FC -4.741) with protective prognosis (Cox log HR -0.358) and IHC literature support. It is a loss-of-identity biomarker, not a target.

limitations.text: No convergent candidate is a selective DepMap dependency; up-regulation and tractability do not imply that tumour cells need the gene.
Purity extrapolation, TCGA replication and single-cell attribution are RNA-based; protein evidence comes only from the CPTAC discovery and confirmatory cohorts.
CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory protein cohort, and HK2 and several other target-profile genes were not run through the confirmatory or single-cell replication layers in this run.
Much of the literature is single-study and bioinformatic; SCARB1, PIGR and FABP6 have no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus.
IMmotion150 arms have about 90 patients each and no gene survives correction for an arm difference; treatment associations are hypotheses.
MGD scores rank structural sites and do not show that a degrader exists; ADC suitability scores do not show that a conjugate would work.
This is a replicate run (runs/replicates/rep1); the ranking depends on chosen weights, and only CA9 is robust in the overall convergence top 10.
